newsitem.title: USA: Thomson Corp unit loses copyright ruling.
newsitem.headline: Thomson Corp unit loses copyright ruling.

text.p: West Publishing Co, a unit of Thomson Corp, has no copyright protection for the decisions of the U.S. Supreme Court and federal appeals courts that it reprints in its legal books, a federal judge has ruled.

Mathew Bender & Co Inc sued West Publishing, challenging the extent of the copyright protection available to West with respect to the opinions of the U.S. Supreme Court and the federal appeals courts.
West publishes the courts' opinions in its Supreme Corut Reporter and Federal Reporter series.
The ruling was handed down on Monday by Judge John Martin Jr of Federal District Court in Manhattan, according to court documents.
Hyperlaw Inc, a publisher of CD-ROM products including one that contains recent Supreme Court cases and one that contains recent appeals court cases, joined the lawsuit as a plaintiff.
Hyperlaw obtains some of the cases in its publications by scanning the title, text and certain other information directly from West's texts.
Martin ruled that Hyperlaw is entitled to copy opinions from the West texts, the court documents showed.
